catalog_quote: En otros dialectos quechuas, el acento es predecible y recae sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra, es decir, no tiene rango fonológico. En cambio, en la variedad santiagueña, el acento es fonológico pues no es predictible. En la inmensa mayoría de los casos cae en la penúltima sílaba, pero existe una serie de voces en las cuales cae en la última; algunas son quichuas como /punčaw/ [punčáw] ‘día', /qollur/ [qožúr] ‘estrella fugaz', pero la mayoría son préstamos de otras lenguas indígenas o hispanismos (/paragway/ [paragwáy], /taŋgol/ [taŋgól], /karaŋ/ [karáŋ], /simbol/ [simból], etc.). Por otra parte, el acento en la última sílaba en ciertas construcciones quichuas es una marca que indica la existencia de un sufijo en grado cero. new_statements.quote: In most Quechua dialects stress is assigned to the penultimate vowel of each polysyllabic word form and thus provides an easy phonology-based criterion for word delimitation. Exceptionally, in interjections and emphatic expressions, stress can be word-final, e.g. in alalaw 'how cold!'. In Tarma and the dialect of northern Junin word-final stress can occur as a result of the elision of a final syllable. [...] In Pacaraos Quechua (see section 3.2.9) stress is phonemic. It may lie either on the penultimate or on the final syllable. [...] More complex, non-penultimate stress patterns, involving word-initial stress and stress dependent on syllable structure, are found in QI Ancash and in QI Cajatambo (cf. Torero 1964: 461; Parker 1976).

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog rule (penultimate stress = penultimate at every length) matches the book's general Quechua statement. The book's Santiago-specific remarks (pp. 187-188: no glottalised/aspirated consonants, retained s/š remnant, alveodental vs alveopalatal fricative after i; p. 197: vowel length taa 'four' citing Kirtchuk 1987) say nothing about stress; no FTS query pairing Santiago del Estero with stress/accent/penultimate/final syllable returned a co-occurring snippet. Copy status: WALS refdb page is a landing page with no PDF; the archive.org copy (languagesofandes0000adel) is controlled lending, could not be reached by automated download; text recovered via the archive.org full-text-search h…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress on the penultimate vowel of every polysyllabic word (a word-delimiting, non-contrastive stress) in most Quechua dialects; Santiago del Estero Quechua is not named among the exceptions, so the general penultimate rule is what the book gives for it.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final stress in interjections and emphatic expressions (alaláw 'how cold!'); word-final stress by elision of a final syllable in Tarma and northern Junín; phonemic penult/final stress in Pacaraos (final with the first-person marker -'y); word-initial and syllable-structure-dependent stress in quantity-insensitive Ancash and quantity-insensitive Cajatambo; 'deviant stress patterns' in QIIA Ferreñafe, QIIB Amazonas and the sixteenth-century coastal dialect. None of these is Santiago del Estero.
new_statements.identity_note: Adelaar & Muysken's stress statement is a family-wide one ('In most Quechua dialects'); their Santiago del Estero (Quechua IIC, 'Santiagueño', speakers called cuzqueros) paragraphs on pp. 187-188 and 197 are segmental only. Yakpo 2018 describes Pichi of Bioko, Equatorial Guinea, not any Quechua variety.

sources.citation: Kirtchuk, Pablo. 1987. Le parler quechua de Santiago del Estero: quelques particularités. Amerindia 12. Paris: A.E.A./CNRS. (journal's re-typeset open PDF, 14 pp.)
sources.quote: 'Le "mot" en quechua est unité phonologique composée d'une ou de plusieurs syllabes dont l'une seulement porte l'accent. Cette syllabe est la pénultième, phonologiquement, et - dans la plupart des dialectes - phonétiquement aussi. ... Or, en QS une syllabe phonétiquement finale peut porter l'accent principal. Dans ce cas, il s'agit du reflet d'une syllabe phonologique qui suit la syllabe accentuée et qui se réalise [ø] ... Ceci est dû à la réduction vocalique de la syllabe post-tonique ... /wasi-pi/ "maison-locatif" peut se réaliser [wasíp]; /wasi-ta/ ... [wasít]; /wasi-man/ ... [wasím].' Fn.1
sources.locator: section 3.6 'Le déplacement de l'accent' (p.7 of the re-typeset file); also fn.10
sources.note: Independent field description with an explicit section on accent placement (penult, surface-final stress from post-tonic suffix apocope); corroborates Alderetes and supplies a second citation for the exceptions mechanism.
